test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 16 March, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'** i.e.** 'Who'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The sentence** says, "Besides, (3) ______ knows if Harvard would even take me now that Charlie’s been suspended."
 
• In **this context,** we need a word that represents an unspecified person.
 
• **Who:** This word is used to refer to a person or people that is previously mentioned or easily identified.
 
• In this case,** 'who'** is used to refer to an unspecified person, fitting the context of the sentence.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *Today I have a college admission interview with a Yale alum. Yale is Second-Best School, but for once, I put my foot down and Refused to apply to Best School (Harvard). The idea of being Charlie’s younger brother at another school is a bridge entirely too far. Besides, **who **knows if Harvard would even take me now that Charlie’s been suspended. My mom and (4) ______ are in the kitchen. Because of my interview, she’s steaming frozen mandu (dumplings) for me as a treat. I am having a pre-mandu appetizer of Cap’n Crunch (the best cereal known to mankind) and (5) ______ in my Moleskine notebook.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Whose: **This word is a possessive form of 'who' and is used to relate a person to something that they own or possess. This does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **Which: **This word is used as a relative pronoun to refer to something previously mentioned when introducing a clause giving further information. It does not fit the context of the sentence as we are referring to an unknown person, not a thing or a specified group of people or things.
 
• **Whom: **This word is a formal term and is used as the object of a verb or preposition to refer to a person or people that is previously mentioned or easily identified. However, it does not fit the context of the sentence as it is not being used as an object.
